clue.text: Good place to begin a race in the far north?

definitions.text: Good place to begin a race

blocks.clueFragment: Good place to begin a race
blocks.note: first meaning: the best starting slot on a motor-racing grid
second meaning, read literally: a location at the North Pole

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether an Arctic start line would suit a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second sense: the racing term read literally as a place at the Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing the front slot on the starting grid, earned by the fastest qualifier, carries this name; literally it is a spot at the Pole.

clue.text: Sacked subordinate made appeal outside

indicators.note: outside says the appeal word wraps around the subordinate word

blocks.note: under someone means subordinate to them
pled is a past form of plead, to make an appeal

explanation.surface: A junior employee who was fired lodged an appeal against the dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacked' looks like dismissed from a job, but it means pillaged; pled is the Scots and American past tense of plead.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to loot it, so a sacked city has been robbed and pillaged by invaders.

clue.text: Seducer showing reluctance over a S American resort

blocks.note: loth means reluctant or unwilling
taken as written
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian beach resort

explanation.surface: A womaniser grudgingly heads off to a South American holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The adjective loth stands for the noun 'reluctance' here; 'over' places it above the rest in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, the rake in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent, became the byword for a man who habitually seduces women.

clue.text: Penny standing on edge - that's very nice

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A coin balanced on its edge is a neat trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing on' places the coin's letter on top in this down entry. 'Nice' here has its old sense of fussy and precise.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in its older sense means fastidious or exacting, and someone prim is stiffly proper about manners.

clue.text: Big shop yielding to pressure

indicators.note: something yielding gives way and changes shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large retailer gives in to pressure from its customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yielding to pressure' reads as one phrase about giving in, but 'to pressure' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A very large out-of-town retail outlet selling a wide range of goods is a big shop of this kind.

clue.text: #Without Vera, her harvest's unlikely to put out grain

indicators.note: Without says the name's letters are taken away from the following word
unlikely suggests an improbable form, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a stray OCR mark on the page, not part of the clue
taken as written
the name to be removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer's wife fears the harvest will fail without her helper Vera.
explanation.walkthrough: Take V, E, R, A out of harvest to leave H, S, T, add her, and rearrange. The comma hides that 'her' is fodder, not Vera's.
explanation.definitionFit: Threshing beats harvested cereal so the edible kernels separate from straw and chaff, releasing the grain.

clue.text: Work over one chum, half-destroyed by drug

indicators.note: half-destroyed means half the word chum is lost and only its second half survives

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
the Roman numeral for one
the back half of this word

explanation.surface: A friend is left half-wrecked after a drug binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places OP above I in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is the narcotic extracted from poppy latex, the source of morphine and heroin.

clue.text: Quick round to avoid tiresome procedure

blocks.note: short as in brief or quick
a round or lap is a circuit

explanation.surface: Someone takes a quick lap to dodge a dull routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, to short-circuit a process is to bypass its usual laborious steps and take a shortcut.

clue.text: Stalk around a favourite howff

blocks.note: first meaning: to linger about a place as a ghost does
second meaning: a place one often frequents

explanation.surface: Someone prowls about their favourite pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Howff is Scots for a regular meeting place or pub, fitting a Scotsman puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to frequent or prowl a place persistently; as a noun it is a place someone visits often.

clue.text: I'm fond of being even-handed

blocks.note: taken as written
partial to something means fond of it

explanation.surface: Someone declares they like being fair to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that being partial is the opposite of being even-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating every side equally without favouritism, as a fair judge or referee should.

clue.text: Transparent element of old picture show

definitions.text: Transparent element of old picture show

blocks.note: surface reading: an obvious part, plain to see
setter's reading: a glass transparency from a Victorian projection show

explanation.surface: Something plainly visible forms part of an old cinema programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transparent' seems to mean obvious, but it means literally see-through: a painted glass plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic-lantern shows projected images from glass plates through a lens, each plate being one of these.

clue.text: Sincere about aiding centre? Try to call again

indicators.note: centre asks for only the middle letters of aiding
about means the sincere word goes around the selected letters

blocks.note: real means genuine or sincere
the two central letters of this word

explanation.surface: A genuine helper at an aid centre keeps phoning back.
explanation.walkthrough: RE(DI)AL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dial a telephone number once more after a failed or engaged call.

clue.text: Bold soldier is newcomer to study

blocks.note: fresh can mean cheeky or bold
a man is a private soldier, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A brash young soldier takes up his studies.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-year student at a university or college is a beginner at higher learning.

clue.text: Excess in fashion when given to guzzling

blocks.note: a glut is an excess or oversupply
tonish is an old word for stylish, from ton, high fashion

explanation.surface: Overindulgence becomes fashionable when everyone takes to gorging.
explanation.walkthrough: TONISH, from French bon ton, is a rare word for modish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inclined to eat greedily and to excess has the habits of a glutton.

clue.text: Drink it with last of whisky for warmth

indicators.note: last of asks for only the final letter of whisky

blocks.note: a cordial is a sweet drink
taken as written
the final letter

explanation.surface: A dram of whisky is recommended to warm you up.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth of manner, friendliness and geniality between people, is what this noun describes.

clue.text: J& Ends in swellings that annoy eye

definitions.text: Ends in swellings that annoy eye

indicators.note: Ends in asks for only the closing letter of each following word

blocks.note: a stray OCR mark on the page, not part of the clue
the last letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: The worst of a sore eye is the swelling at the lid's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: The page has stray marks 'J&' before the clue. The whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A small inflamed swelling on the edge of the eyelid, caused by an infected gland, is a classic eye irritation.

clue.text: Halt rot in organisation of athletic contest

indicators.note: organisation means putting the letters into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Officials vow to stop the decay in how a sports event is run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does double work in the surface but is just letters in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A triathlon is an endurance race combining swimming, cycling and running in sequence.

clue.text: Took what's offered. Its customary

blocks.note: first meaning: received something given
second meaning: generally approved as usual

explanation.surface: Someone took what was on offer, as is the done thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its' is the printed 'It's', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a past verb it means received willingly; as an adjective it means generally recognised as normal or proper.

clue.text: Went by bicycle track, | hear

indicators.note: hear tells the solver to go by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: a road is a track

explanation.surface: A cyclist travelled along a track.
explanation.walkthrough: The page shows a stray '|' before 'hear'.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of ride, as in travelling on a bike or horse.

clue.text: Appeal for effort after tart's ruined

indicators.note: ruined means the word is wrecked and its letters scrambled

blocks.note: the word without its possessive
action is effort or activity

explanation.surface: A baker pleads for more effort after a pastry goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts ACTION behind the rearranged pastry word.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeal as a noun means allure or charm, the quality of drawing people in.

clue.text: Passion from which we regard ourselves free

indicators.note: from which says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

blocks.note: found running across the two words
surface padding completing the sentence

explanation.surface: A feeling we consider ourselves free of.
explanation.walkthrough: reg(ARD OUR)selves; 'we' and 'free' are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is intense enthusiasm or burning devotion, a synonym for passion.

clue.text: Manoeuvring round wet recoil from wave

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving pieces around into a new position

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boat steers around in wet weather as waves pull back.
explanation.definitionFit: The current flowing seaward beneath breaking surf is the backward pull of water after a wave hits the shore.

clue.text: Leave drain to go into sea

blocks.note: first meaning: to abandon or dump
second meaning: a channel dug to carry away water
a third sense: an aircraft crash-landing on water

explanation.surface: Water left in a drain flows out into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Really three senses: abandon, a drainage trench, and to make an emergency landing on water.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means abandon; as a noun it is a narrow trench dug for drainage beside fields or roads.

clue.text: Joyous bit of old wife's tale

indicators.note: bit of says the letters form only a fragment of the following words

blocks.note: found spanning two of these words

explanation.surface: A cheerful snippet from an old wives' tale.
explanation.walkthrough: wi(FE'S TAL)e.
explanation.definitionFit: Festal means relating to a feast or festival, hence merry and celebratory.

clue.text: It leads to arched portico within

indicators.note: within says the letters lie inside the preceding words

blocks.note: found across three of these words

explanation.surface: A doorway opens onto an arched porch.
explanation.walkthrough: lead(S TO A)rched.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered colonnade in ancient Greek architecture, a roofed walkway with columns.

clue.text: Exterior decorator, with designs to hide

definitions.text: Exterior decorator, with designs to hide

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who paints the outside of houses
setter's reading: an artist who decorates skin, the body's exterior, with designs

explanation.surface: A house painter with secret plans to conceal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a verb, conceal, but is the noun: skin.
explanation.definitionFit: This artist inks permanent pictures and patterns into people's skin for a living.

clue.text: Bound to include touch of lagging like many roofs

indicators.note: touch of asks for just the opening letter of lagging
to include says the bound word takes the selected letter inside it

blocks.note: tied means bound
the first letter

explanation.surface: Insulation tied up around a roof, as is common.
explanation.walkthrough: Lagging is insulation wrapped around pipes or lofts; only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Many roofs are covered with overlapping slate or clay tiles, so they are tiled.

clue.text: Pipe for one keeping away from tobacco

blocks.clueFragment: Pipe for one keeping away from tobacco
blocks.note: surface reading: a pipe for someone who abstains from smoking
setter's reading: a pipe whose very long stem keeps the smoker's face far from the burning bowl

explanation.surface: A pipe for someone who is giving up smoking.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also a parish officer, which the surface hints at with its abstinent air.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe is named after the parish officers once said to favour it.
